content: Pulse Asia, Inc. is an organization in the Philippines that specializes in public opinion polling. It was established by a group of professional academics who are recognized as experts in their respective fields. The organization focuses on monitoring significant socio-economic, political, and cultural issues that are of concern to the Filipino public. According to its corporate profile, Pulse Asia views the public's opinion as a critical component of a functioning democracy. The organization is dedicated to advancing professional polling conducted by Filipinos, both within the Philippines and across other parts of Asia. It employs careful and academically rigorous methods to innovate in the collection, utilization, and analysis of social data. Additionally, it explores new or under-researched areas of study that are of substantial relevance or interest to the public. Pulse Asia operates with academic independence and is supported by a highly skilled professional team. It initiates its own research studies based on regular monitoring of key public concerns at national, regional, local, or sectoral levels. The organization also seeks third-party sponsorships or subscriptions for its research outputs and may conduct specific surveys upon request. However, it does not engage in proprietary surveys where the client retains exclusive rights to the findings and withholds them from the public indefinitely. All surveys conducted by Pulse Asia are made publicly available within one year of their release to a client. The organization is committed to serving the public interest in democratic governance by conducting studies on social, economic, political, and policy issues. It ensures that the findings, analyses, and policy recommendations from its independent, non-partisan, and academic investigations are accessible to the widest possible audience. Pulse Asia adheres to the following principles: (1) all work must meet the generally accepted standards of quality academic output; (2) all studies automatically become public domain material within one year of completion to facilitate public access to information; and (3) it provides equitable access to information by assisting parties or individuals who cannot adequately finance their critical information needs. The team of analysts at Pulse Asia includes distinguished professionals such as: Prof. Felipe B. Miranda, a political science professor at the University of the Philippines and a founding fellow of the Social Weather Stations. Mercedes R. Abad, president and general manager of TRENDS-MBL, Inc. Jose V. Abueva, former president of the University of the Philippines and current president of Kalayaan College. Arsenio M. Balisacan, a professor of economics at the University of the Philippines. Maria Rose Cynthia Banzon-Bautista, a sociology professor at the University of the Philippines. Emmanuel S. de Dios, former chairman of the Department of Economics at the University of the Philippines School of Economics. Ronald D. Holmes, executive director of the De La Salle University System and director of the De La Salle-Santiago Zobel School. Jose P. de Jesus, a prominent technocrat who has served the Philippine government in various capacities. Romeo L. Manlapaz, a mathematics professor at the University of the Philippines. Rosa Linda Tidalgo Miranda, executive director of the Center for Asia-Pacific Women in Politics. Temario C. Rivera, a political science professor at the University of the Philippines. Ana Maria L. Tabunda, dean of the University of the Philippines School of Statistics. Zelda C. Zablan, a professor of demography at the UP Population Institute. In June 2006, Pulse Asia conducted a pre-election poll for the 2007 elections. The results indicated that the survey slots were predominantly in favor of the political opposition.
